about: Tempo grid, bar lines, segment positions, key/chords and rough sung pitches of v2_2 (first AI take, FULL MIX only: no separated vocal exists yet). All times in seconds on the timeline of v2_2.mp3 decoded by ffmpeg (44.1 kHz mono; ffmpeg removes the mp3 encoder delay).

inputs.mix: v2_2.mp3 (48 kHz stereo mp3, 105.0 s; decoded with ffmpeg to 44.1 kHz mono)

summary.bpm_note: machine grid at 105.00 BPM (refined lattice 105.003 +- 0.001 on the decoded mp3; an exact 105.000 grid drifts only 2.7 ms over 100 s). The value 104.96 guessed from the word timestamps was a rounding effect of their 20 ms grid.
summary.meter: 4/4; kick on every beat (four on the floor), hats/chord strum on the off-beat eighths; verse = 24 beats = 6 bars
summary.beat_formula: beat n at phase_first_beat_s + n*beat_sec ; verse v (1..7) downbeat = beat 15 + 24*(v-1)
summary.statement_segments: All 35 segments start on their expected beat: L1, L2, ses and L4 on the downbeat of bars 0,1,2,3 of the verse, "diye bagirir" on beat 2 of bar 2 (offset 2.0 beats). No pickups. L1 ("Ali", vowel) sits within about +-20 ms of the bar line (median -2 ms). L2 and L4 begin with the fricative "c" of "ciftliginde", whose noise starts 25-45 ms (L2) and 37-62 ms (L4) BEFORE the bar line, so that the vowel lands on the beat. "diye" starts on beat 2 of its bar, 0 to +31 ms late (median +9 ms). The sung animal sounds start -37..+16 ms around the bar line (words file only).
summary.original_key_confidence: high for the chord roots and the loop (identical in all 42 bars), medium-high for the chord qualities (Gm and C clear; minor third of Dm and major third of A weak but consistent)
summary.original_chord_loop: Dm - C - Gm - A, two beats each, i.e. a 2-bar loop | Dm C | Gm A | that runs three times per verse and restarts on Dm exactly at every verse downbeat
summary.chords_per_bar: bar 0: Dm (beats 0-1) C (beats 2-3) | bar 1: Gm (beats 0-1) A (beats 2-3) | bar 2: Dm (beats 0-1) C (beats 2-3) | bar 3: Gm (beats 0-1) A (beats 2-3) | bar 4: Dm (beats 0-1) C (beats 2-3) | bar 5: Gm (beats 0-1) A (beats 2-3)
summary.tuning_note: about +2..+6 cents, i.e. standard A=440 within measurement error (bass-register peaks +3.7/+5.5, mid register +1.7, librosa +4)
summary.sung_pitch_classes: D E F G A (D4..A4); F natural is sung in every verse ("bagirir" G-F-E, the animal word E/F, last line F-E-D). The vocal is NOT the traditional Old MacDonald tune and was composed over D minor harmony.
summary.key_for_new_backing_reason: The task offered G major or C major. All five sung pitch classes D E F G A are inside C major; in G major the sung F natural (about 15 % of the sung time, present in 7/7 verses) is outside the scale and collides with the F sharp of the V7 chord. Fit score under the planned harmony I I IV I: C major 0.71, F major 0.61, G major 0.60 (D minor original loop key for reference 0.69).
summary.key_for_new_backing_confidence: medium-high that C major fits better than G major; MEDIUM that the result is pleasant at all, because the vocal was written over Dm-C-Gm-A: in C major the lines L2 and L4 end on D (= re, not the tonic) and the sung F is a suspended fourth against the E of the C chord. Not checked by ear.
summary.confidence: tempo, beat phase and constancy: high. Bar lines at the verse onsets: high (band entry, 24-beat verse period, 2-bar chord loop restarting on the tonic chord there); beat 1 rather than beat 3: medium-high (no drum accent to prove it; harmonic rhythm supports it). Segment offsets: +-10 ms where refined on the mix, +-25 ms where only the words file was available (see refined_reliable). Nothing was checked by ear.

method_A_fullband_spectral_flux.description: onset envelope = half-wave rectified log-magnitude spectral flux 30 Hz-16 kHz (hop 5.8 ms); (BPM, phase) maximising the mean envelope on the beat grid; autocorrelation as cross-check

method_B_kick_lowfreq_40_120Hz.description: kick band 40-120 Hz amplitude envelope, log-rise half-wave rectified; same grid search and autocorrelation

method_C_hats_8_16kHz_flux.description: spectral flux 8-16 kHz (hats/shaker); locks to the off-beat eighth

third_opinion_librosa_beat_track.note: librosa quantises to its 5.8 ms hop and locks to the OFF-beat eighth (phase 0.297 s = half a beat + 11 ms); its linear-fit tempo over the body is 105.00

per_window_summary.note: window search step 0.02 BPM; a 20 s window resolves about +-0.03 BPM. Two A windows lock to the off-beat eighth (deviation about half a beat); folded to the eighth-note lattice they agree within 2 ms.

fine_drift_check.description: 10 s windows every 5 s: position (ms) of the steepest rise of full-rate band envelopes folded over an exact 105.000 BPM beat; a straight line = constant tempo, slope = tempo correction

refined_lattice.definition: beat time = steepest rise of the on-beat transient (kick click / attack in the bands 120 Hz-16 kHz); the kick low-frequency body (40-120 Hz) rises about 25 ms later

vocal_only_from_words_file.note: 35 segment onsets of the words file regressed on lattice beat numbers

result.statement: Tempo is constant (machine grid): 105.00 BPM. Methods A, B, C, librosa and the words-file regression (104.99) agree; no window deviates by more than 0.06 BPM (window resolution) and the beat phase stays within +-3 ms of one straight lattice over the whole song. Use exactly 105.0 BPM for the new backing (bar = 2.285714 s).

methods_compared.statement: Full-band flux (A, -3 ms) and kick low-frequency rise (B, +4 ms) pick the SAME beat phase: the eighth that carries the kick. Hats (C) and librosa pick the other eighth (off-beat), 4 ms / 11 ms off the exact half beat. Beat = kick eighth.

beat_phase.per_verse_note: steepest rise of the on-beat attack inside the 24 beats of each verse minus the global lattice: 120-300 Hz +2.0..+4.7 ms, 300-2000 Hz -0.2..-1.2 ms, no trend -> one global lattice is valid for every verse

downbeat.irregularities: None inside the song body: all six verse-to-verse distances are exactly 24 beats (6 bars); every verse = 4 sung bars + 2 instrumental bars. Only the INTRO is odd: 15 beats (not 16) before verse 1, i.e. the audio starts on beat 2 of a 4-bar intro (bar lines of the intro at 1.714, 4.000, 6.286 s); the intro has no kick and no chords, only off-beat percussion.

evidence.E1_band_entry: kick (40-120 Hz) and the chord instrument are absent in beats 0-14 (level about 0.05 of the body) and enter together exactly on beat 15 = first syllable of verse 1
evidence.E2_verse_period: beat-feature self-similarity is by far highest at lag 24 beats (0.59; lag 4: 0.17, lag 8: 0.07); the vocal (4 bars) / instrumental (2 bars) change happens at position 16 = a multiple of 4 (overall level drops from about 1.05 to 0.8 there)
evidence.E3_harmonic_rhythm: chord loop Dm C | Gm A (2 beats per chord) starts on the tonic chord Dm at positions 0, 8, 16 of every verse and the dominant A fills the last two beats before each of them
evidence.E4_lyrics: the five sung units start at positions 0.0, 4.0, 8.0, 10.0 and 12.0 beats from the verse onset (medians [0.026, 3.97, 7.96, 10.012, 11.958])
evidence.E5_weak: drums give no bar accent (kick on every beat, same hats); nothing separates "verse onset = beat 1" from "= beat 3" except E1-E3

confidence.bar_lines_at_verse_onsets_and_every_4_be: high (medium-high for beat 1 vs beat 3, which does not matter for re-placing the segments)

onset_definitions.onset: start of the first word of the segment. Where refined_reliable is true: first time after the preceding energy dip at which the band-subtracted mix envelope (300-3400 Hz for vowel/voiced starts, 2-7 kHz for "c" starts; band = 90th percentile of the same beat phase in the instrumental bars) reaches 25 % of the first-syllable peak. Otherwise the words-file start (20 ms grid).
onset_definitions.end: end of the last word of the segment from the words file (not refined; reverb/breath tails are not included)
onset_definitions.bar_downbeat: lattice time of the downbeat of the bar the segment belongs to: verse downbeat + 4 beats x bar_in_verse (L1 bar 0, L2 bar 1, ses bar 2, diye bar 2, L4 bar 3)
onset_definitions.offset: offset_sec = onset - bar_downbeat; offset_beats = offset_sec / beat period. For "diye" the expected value is 2 beats; deviation_from_expected_beat_ms removes that.
onset_definitions.accuracy: refined onsets about +-10 ms; words-file onsets about +-25 ms; bar_downbeat about +-3 ms relative to the drum transients

gaps_between_segments_for_cutting_ms.note: from the words file: L2 runs straight into the sung animal sound (0-40 ms gap) and "diye" follows the second animal sound after 100-340 ms; the sung animal sounds therefore cannot be cut out on silence everywhere, cross-fades of a few tens of ms will be needed (to be checked on the separated vocal)

key.statement: The ORIGINAL band of v2_2 is in D minor (not G major, not C major): 2-bar loop Dm - C - Gm - A (i - VII - iv - V), two beats per chord, identical in all six bars of every verse and in the instrumental bars.
key.how: No bass guitar exists: 40-120 Hz is only the kick (about 52 Hz). The chord instrument plays on the off-beat half of each beat with its lowest notes A2..G3 (95-275 Hz), below the sung range, so root/fifth are read there without vocal interference: A2+D3(+F3) = Dm, C3+G3 (+E in the mid register) = C, G/Bb2/D3/F3 = Gm (Bb is the strongest low partial), A2+E3 (+C#) = A.
key.chords_text: bar 0: Dm (beats 0-1) C (beats 2-3) | bar 1: Gm (beats 0-1) A (beats 2-3) | bar 2: Dm (beats 0-1) C (beats 2-3) | bar 3: Gm (beats 0-1) A (beats 2-3) | bar 4: Dm (beats 0-1) C (beats 2-3) | bar 5: Gm (beats 0-1) A (beats 2-3)
key.scale: D natural minor (D E F G A Bb C) with C# only inside the dominant A chord; relative major F major
key.krumhansl_note: global key-profile correlation is NOT reliable here (the note A dominates the low register as fifth of Dm and root of A; the mid register is dominated by the vocal) - it is reported only for completeness; the decision rests on the chord loop

confidence.roots_and_loop: high (per-verse votes agree in 5-7 of 7 verses for every half bar, 7/7 in the vocal-free bars)
confidence.chord_quality: Gm high (Bb), C high (E), Dm medium-high (F weak but present, no F#), A medium (C# weak; in the last beat of the loop a D sounds on top = Asus4 or anticipation of Dm)

low_register_notes_per_beat_from_10_bass.note: strongest harmonic-sum note 36-135 Hz per beat (it is the LOWEST chord note, not a bass line): A A C G/A | C C A G | ... consistent with the loop above

vocal_pitch_rough.flag: ROUGH: measured on the full mix; the band (off-beat chords and melody notes in the same register) is still in the signal
vocal_pitch_rough.method: harmonic-comb salience (harmonics 1-5) on a 93 ms STFT, 10 ms hop, 130-700 Hz, per word: median, stable note runs, frame share; cross-check pyworld harvest on the 200-1500 Hz band. Octave is uncertain by construction (G3 results for "bir"/"diye" are octave errors of G4, pyworld gives G4).
vocal_pitch_rough.melody_summary: L1: D4 (Ali, rising to G4) A4 (Baba'nin) G4 (bir) G4-F4 (ciftligi) E4 (var) | L2: D4-G4 (ciftliginde) F4/E4 alternating (animal word) D4 (var) | ses: D4, A4 | diye G4, bagirir G4-F4-E4 | L4: D4-G4 (ciftliginde) F4-E4 (Ali) F4-E4-D4 (Baba'nin)

key_fit_for_new_backing.method: duration-weighted: chord tone 1, scale tone 0.5, avoid note (semitone above a chord tone) 0, outside scale -1; harmony I I IV I per beat for L1/L2/L4 bars, I for diye bagirir

ranking.key: D minor (original loop key, for reference: i i iv i)

timeline_note: Bar lines and onsets are on the timeline of v2_2.mp3 as decoded by ffmpeg. A separated vocal file can be shifted by a few ms and can run some tens of ppm faster/slower (the previous take: -4 ms, 78 ppm): re-measure the lag before cutting (method: yeni3/analiz/tempo/kod/09_align_fine.py and 12_align_spectro.py).
not_verified: No listening was possible. Everything above is measurement on the full mix. Unverified by ear: that the bar lines feel right, that the refined onsets are the perceived starts, the octave and exact notes of the sung melody, and above all that the D-minor vocal sounds acceptable over a C major (or any major) backing with the traditional tune.
reproduce: run kod/run_all.sh; intermediate results: tempo_step1.json, phase_fine.json, drift_fine.json, lattice.json, downbeat_evidence.json, bass_notes.json, key_chords.json, segments.json, vocal_pitch_rough.json
